Question_text: APQ is a multinational company. It makes chemicals that are sold to farmers which help increase the amount of food produced. It plans to open a factory in country X, a developing country with low interest rates. The Finance Director said: ‘This factory will create many external benefits. APQ is a public limited company which tries to act in an ethical way with all its stakeholder groups.' The new factory will cost $100m and there will be an opportunity cost for APQ. The Finance Director cannot decide which source of finance to use for the new factory.
Sub_topic: Benefits to country/economy: jobs, exports, choice, investment
Concepts of needs, wants, scarcity, opportunity cost
Ethical issues: profit vs ethics conflicts
Factors in choice: size, legal form, amount, time, loans
Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'opportunity cost'?
Identify two possible external benefits that might result from the new factory.
Identify and explain two advantages to APQ of being a multinational company.
Identify two stakeholder groups of APQ. Explain how APQ could act in an ethical way with each stakeholder group.
Explain two suitable sources of finance that APQ could use for the new factory. Recommend which source of finance APQ should use. Justify your answer.

Question_text: $LAND sells a wide range of products from food to toys. It has 400 shops in country B. $LAND's marketing strategy is based on penetration pricing. $LAND does no advertising and buys all its products directly from manufacturers. Revenue and profit have increased despite the country being in recession. The Marketing Director wants to expand the business by opening shops in other countries. He believes $LAND will be successful in other countries.
Sub_topic: Advantages, disadvantages of channels: wholesalers, retailers, direct
Forms: advertising, sales promotion, influence on sales
Importance of marketing mix elements in decisions
Opportunities of foreign markets: growth potential
Pricing methods: cost plus, competitive, penetration, skimming, promotional
Problems: cultural differences, lack of knowledge

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'marketing strategy'?
What is meant by 'penetration pricing'?
Identify and explain two possible advantages to $LAND of advertising.
Identify and explain one advantage and one disadvantage to $LAND of buying direct from manufacturers.
Do you think that $LAND will be successful in other countries? Justify your answer.

He believes good internal communication can help TKF be more efficient. The manager is also worried about TKF's cash flow position. After researching different types of business organisation, as shown in Table 2, Moeen thinks the hotel should be a private limited company. If the business is to be successful, Ali knows choosing the right location will be important. He cannot decide whether to recruit full-time or part-time employees.
